title: Chromate-Free Surface Protection Standard for Metallic Fuselage and Wing Joints
abstract: Replacement of chromated conversion coatings and primers on metallic airframe joints by a chromate-free process, driven by the restriction on hexavalent chromium and validated against the existing corrosion and adhesion requirements.

sections.reason: Authorisation for the continued industrial use of hexavalent chromium in conversion coatings and primers expires progressively across the supply chain, and several detail-part suppliers have already stopped offering the chromated process. Continuing to specify it would create a single-source dependency on two remaining plants and would leave repair stations without a compliant process for joints they are required to re-protect after any structural work. The change was launched on obsolescence grounds rather than in response to any in-service finding.
sections.description: The conversion coating and primer specification for metallic faying surfaces on fuselage and wing joints is replaced by a chromate-free system consisting of a trivalent chromium conversion coating and a chromate-free epoxy primer. The process is qualified on the surface treatment reference articles D5120112339055 and D5120116861898, which are used as coupon carriers during process validation at each site. The grommet AES445369-54 is superseded because its silicone compound is incompatible with the new primer cure cycle. Drawing D51201131570 issue H carries the revised process sheet, the cure schedule and the adhesion test acceptance criteria. Sealant selection is unchanged. The change applies to new build and to any joint opened during repair or modification, and it introduces a mandatory adhesion coupon per shift for the first six months at each embodying site.
sections.effects: No mass or balance change. No electrical load change. The two protection systems are interchangeable at joint level, but a single faying surface must not carry both, so any joint opened after cut-in is fully converted rather than touched up. Salt spray performance is equivalent and filiform resistance is marginally better; adhesion after humidity ageing is slightly lower, which is why an adhesion coupon is required. Standard practices content for ATA 51-20 was re-issued and repair station approvals had to be extended before the process could be used outside the production line.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN Z11538 in October 2023. Availability for in-service work is through the standard practices bulletin, which releases the process to repair stations that hold the extended approval. There is no aircraft-level kit; embodiment is recorded per joint.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z11538, absorbed within the existing surface treatment line with a six-month dual-process period

issue.reason: The site readiness dates for the chromate-free process are taken from the surface protection approval register and stated in the embodiment note.

Any retrofit programme whose faying surface is protected with this system takes its earliest start date from that register.
